summary: All three runs read as plausible sets of company accounts for the businesses described: construction turnover with sub-contractor and materials cost of sales, payroll, depreciation on the new plant, and VAT boxes that behave as the scenario states (nil for the unregistered company, £7,809 for the registered one). The IT consultancy run also hangs together, with two presentational/computational oddities worth a look but nothing that undermines the story the accounts tell.

concerns.figure: Materials / Stock (code s) £15,500 in the P&L against a purchase journal of £15,000 coded s
concerns.where: ltd-brickwork-pro-nonvat, Profit & Loss Account, Cost of Sales
concerns.why: The extra £500 is the stock loss adjustment (opening 3,000 less closing count 2,500) flowing through cost of sales, so it reconciles; noted only so a reader who compares the journal code total to the line is not surprised. Same pattern in the VAT run (£23,000 against £22,500 coded s).

concerns.figure: Marginal relief warning: expected £36,880, actual corporation tax £28,028.78
concerns.where: ltd-scenario-full, Compliance Checks final row and Corporation Tax (CT600) section
concerns.why: Profit chargeable of £147,520 is above the £50k lower limit, so the workbook applies a rate below the main rate. The report already flags this as a warning and the deterministic checks tie the CT600 boxes together; it is a tax-rate question for a person, not a broken figure.

concerns.figure: Profit Before Tax £177,215.39 in the management P&L against £177,279.90 in the Published P&L
concerns.where: ltd-scenario-full, Profit & Loss Account vs Published P&L
concerns.why: The two statements differ by £64.51, which is the tax deducted at source on bank interest (CorporationTax K37 / CT600 AJ154); the published sheet uses gross interest of £339.51 while the management P&L uses net £275. Presentational, but a reader will notice two different PBT figures in the same pack.

concerns.figure: Directors Loan £13,000 and Other Creditors £13,000 both shown below Total Assets less CL
concerns.why: The same £13,000 appears on two adjacent lines, yet Net Assets is £195,053.12 = £208,053.12 less £13,000, so only one deduction is made. The layout duplicates the label rather than the amount; worth confirming the sheet's presentation of long-term creditors.

concerns.figure: Corporation tax for the year £1,514.11 in the fixed asset note against CT600 tax payable £756.02
concerns.where: ltd-brickwork-pro-vat, Fixed Asset Note and CT600 cells AJ126/AJ131
concerns.why: The note carries roughly double the CT600 figure because the working sheet apportions the chargeable profit across two financial years (I33 £756.02 + I34 £758.09 = £1,514.11) while the CT600 boxes show only the first year's slice. The total charged to the accounts is the correct £1,514.11, so it reconciles, but the CT600 boxes read low for the year.
